global_issues.title: Taiwan, US Push Stricter AI Chip Export Controls
global_issues.note: Directionally correct but stale/imprecise. Taiwan's push for stricter AI chip export rules dates to a policy discussion from June 2026, not a fresh Sep 12-13 development. The ASML 'best machine smuggled to China' claim is a real, still-unresolved dispute (US commerce secretary raised it with ASML; ASML flatly denies it, no public evidence) — briefing correctly frames it as 'reportedly'/'suspects' but doesn't note ASML's denial. Also omits the more concrete and market-moving related story: TSMC's confirmed 2027 chip price hike (5-10%+ on HPC), which is a bigger near-term driver for TSM/NVDA than the export-control chatter.

grok_report.summary: Watchlist price levels (NVDA $218.29, TSM $433.24 +1.22%, ANET move) check out against the last completed trading session (Friday Sep 11 — Sep 12/13 were weekend), and sector leader/laggard calls are reasonable. However, the briefing misses the two biggest market-moving stories of the period — the US-Iran conflict pushing oil above $100/barrel and a Fed decision that has flipped toward a possible rate hike — both of which materially undercut the 'yellow, constructive regime' mood framing.
